## Summary

    Create a fork of a repository.
    
    With no argument, creates a fork of the current repository. Otherwise, forks the specified repository.
    
    Usage:
      gh repo fork [<repository>] [flags]
    
    Flags:
      -n, --no    Run non-interactively, saying no to prompts
      -y, --yes   Run non-interactively, saying yes to prompts

From outside a cloned repo:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98482/75293159-3e289700-57eb-11ea-80a0-aa4a20f85f08.png)

From inside a cloned repo:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98482/75293310-8c3d9a80-57eb-11ea-8be3-2f2913f5303e.png)

- Prompts about either adding a remote (when run from a repo directory) or cloning new fork (when run not in a repo directory)
- Uses https for remotes for now
- Allows non-interactive use with -y and -n

closes #334
pr_comments: Woo this is looking great! This was the formatting and language I had in mind: From outside cloned repo: From inside cloned repo: I know we haven't included all of these unicode characters before so no worries if we want to add that in later!

![spinner](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98482/75372806-b09e8300-588e-11ea-89a1-5be7d28d2ffa.gif)

Oh one last thing, should we output the fork URL at any point?

hm, I feel like someone's next action is going to be editing code or doing something git-related so I feel like the URL isn't super necessary? I'd be curious to leave it out and see if there's a request.

issue_context.title: Add explicit ability to fork a repo
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

Currently, we help people create a fork if they don't have one in the `gh pr create` command, but this isn't particularly discoverable as we've heard requests for an explicit ability to fork a repo.

### Proposed solution

`gh repo fork` with no args: fork the repo I'm currently in
`gh repo fork [repo]`: fork the repo specified, supporting owner/repo and URL
comments: I am interested in this :slightly_smiling_face: but is it just me or I can't find a note on how to fork a repository using the GraphQL API? I only find it on the [REST API](https://developer.github.com/v3/repos/forks/#create-a-fork). Should I just use the REST one?
Hi @joshuabezaleel, this is something that our team is going to take on in the next few weeks, so we're not looking for contributions for it. Thanks!

I've gotten forking working; I stopped short of automatically adding remotes or cloning. It seemed like we'd have to guess at too much user intent, so as a discussion point I'm suggesting copy-pastable next steps:

from inside a repo:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98482/75196635-06a1e800-5722-11ea-9989-946515395f5e.png)

from outside a repo:
![outside](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98482/75196695-22a58980-5722-11ea-8a1c-fc79142bea92.png)

Off the top of my head, some options:

- leave this as is
- add a remote when calling from within repo
  - name it `fork` **or** prompt for a name
- clone when calling from outside repo, maybe asking if it's what they want first

NB: will suggest `gh clone` once that exists :)

@vilmibm Thanks! A few thoughts here (cc: @ampinsk as well):

1. I think this is a great start and would be fine shipping this as a v1
2. I'm inclined to offer to do a bit more for people, so in the first example from within a repo, maybe create the fork and then offer to add the remote where they can just say Y/n?
3. Since this is going to be released alongside `gh repo clone`, I'm also inclined to offer that as the "Clone the new fork" in the second example

My biggest questions are:

1. Where do you end up locally after you create the fork? 
2. Are we creating a separate local version as well if you fork a repo while you're in it, and if so, do we take you there? And I assume the fork directory would need to live outside the parent locally to keep Git happy, so do we handle that for people?

>  Where do you end up locally after you create the fork?

Exactly where you started; the only state that has changed is on GitHub.

> Are we creating a separate local version as well if you fork a repo while you're in it, and if so, do we take you there? And I assume the fork directory would need to live outside the parent locally to keep Git happy, so do we handle that for people?

No. If you fork a repo that you've already cloned, it creates the fork on GitHub and takes no action locally; I think it would be very confusing to re-clone the fork instead of just adding a remote in this case.

Maybe something like this when run implicitly:

    cd ~/code/coolproject
    gh repo fork
    Forking rad/coolproject...
    rad/coolproject successfully forked to vilmibm/coolproject!
    Would you like to add a remote called fork? [Yne] e
    What would you like to call the remote? vilmibm
    git remote add vilmibm git@github.com:vilmibm/coolproject
    git fetch vilmibm
    Successfully added remote vilmibm.

And something like this for when run explicitly:

    cd ~/code/
    gh repo fork rad/coolproject
    Forking rad/coolproject...
    rad/coolproject successfully forked to vilmibm/coolproject!
    Would you like to clone the fork now? [Yn] y
    git clone git@github.com:vilmibm/coolproject
    Fork cloned locally.

With support for `-y` to run non-interactively saying yes to prompts and `-n` to run non-interactively to say no to prompts.

TIL `NoOptDefVal`!

I wonder, though, if the users will understand that the default value for `--clone` _omitted_ is "prompt" (as indicated in help docs), but that the default value for `--clone` _passed_ without value is "true" 🤔

@mislav Yep, same ambivalence as you here, and @ampinsk and @vilmibm went back and forth on it starting here: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/549#discussion_r384823866

It didn't seem like anything we thought of was obviously very elegant, but this feels like a reasonable starting point at least to me and we can always update it if we see evidence of confusion.
I wonder if there should exist a shared variant of `FromFullName` that raises an error like this so we can consistently parse user input with that
I do think FromFullName should be stricter; I can't think of a time when an empty owner or name is anything but an error.
